items.title: How I built this portfolio, and what made it lag
items.summary: A Surface Pro and an ESP32 in 3D, an ocean background, liquid glass. Here is what the page is made of and the one thing that nearly broke it.
items.body:
This site is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No framework, no build step. The 3D laptop is Three.js, and the ESP32 next to it is my own XIAO ESP32-S3, converted from its STEP file into a web model.

## Two fonts, on purpose

Geist Pixel does the system voice: labels, buttons, body text. Redaction 35 does the headings. Two typefaces with very different personalities give the page contrast without adding colour.

## The lag

I wanted every panel to look like liquid glass, which usually means a blur behind each one. The catch is that a blur re-blurs whatever moves behind it, on every frame. With a 3D scene, scrolling bands and an ocean behind dozens of panels, the page slowed to a crawl.

The fix was to stop blurring everywhere. The panels keep the rim light, the inner glow and a stronger tint, and almost nobody can tell the difference. The expensive blur is now opt-in.

> Measure first. The thing I assumed was slow was not the thing that was slow.

## The easter egg

Click the laptop, or type arch, and the screen runs fastfetch for a Surface Pro on Arch Linux ARM, then morphs it into big ASCII letters. I will not spoil the last line.

items.title: Hello, world: I build hardware that talks to software
items.summary: Who I am, what I am building right now, and why I wrote the firmware for a brain-signal headband.
items.body:
I am Uday, a student developer from Vadodara, India. Firmware and hardware are my favourite part of any build: the moment a sensor reading turns into something you can see on a screen.

In 2026 I competed at WRO Future Innovators with team CultureWear, as the primary firmware and hardware developer. I also wrote the firmware for Samata, a wearable EEG and IMU headband built for WRO Nationals.

Right now I am fully focused on Knowura, an education AI app. I will use this space to write about what I learn along the way.
